stories.title: Zverev to face Alcaraz in the championship match at the ATP Finals in a test of his No. 1 ranking
stories.summary: TURIN, Italy (AP) — Alexander Zverev has faced criticism for weeks about ascending to the No. 1 ranking without beating Carlos Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner — without even facing them, actually, en route to his first two Grand Slam titles.

stories.title: Quebec students are considering a general strike to protest affordability crisis
stories.summary: MONTREAL — College and university students are gathering in Montreal on Saturday to discuss and vote on the possibility of launching an indefinite general strike during their winter semester.

stories.title: 24 dead in Nigeria when boat capsizes while carrying people to a funeral
stories.summary: ABUJA, Nigeria (AP) — A boat carrying people to a funeral has capsized in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people, emergency services said on Saturday.

stories.title: U.S. senator says Hegseth memo does not change military co-operation with Canada
stories.summary: HALIFAX — A Republican senator says a U.S. defence department’s memo that reportedly placed restrictions on co-operation with Canada applies to things such as participating in think-tank conferences, not military operations. Sen.

stories.title: 11 killed in burst of violence in northern Mexico after capture of cartel leader
stories.summary: GUASAVE, Mexico (AP) — A burst of violence in Mexico’s Sinaloa state after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” left at least 11 people dead, authorities said Saturday.

stories.title: A study commissioned by Alto finds it would add $24.5 billion annually to the GDP
stories.summary: MONTREAL — A high-speed train line between Quebec City and Toronto would add $24.5 billion annually to Canada’s GDP, primarily due to productivity gains, according to a recent study commissioned by Alto.

stories.title: Japanese figure skater Mao Shimada wins a second Grand Prix in her debut season
stories.summary: HELSINKI, Finland (AP) — Mao Shimada of Japan won the Finlandia Trophy Grand Prix on Saturday, making it two-of-two for the 18-year-old in her first senior-level figure skating season.

stories.title: Alberta's Smith says amendments coming to proposed bike lane legislation
stories.summary: EDMONTON — Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said Saturday her government is planning to make changes to its proposed bike lane legislation just two days after it was tabled in the legislature.
